step1_analysis.description: A high-efficiency switching power amplifier that utilizes a resonant load network to achieve zero-voltage switching (ZVS). The provided netlist contains the main switching transistor (XM1), which requires an external RF choke, shunt capacitor, and series LC resonator to operate in Class-E mode.

paper_reference.title: A High Efficiency Broadband Class-E Power Amplifier Using a Reactance Compensation Technique

Operating Frequency.description: The frequency of the RF input signal at which the PA is designed to operate.

sky130_expected.calculation: Selected based on the fT of the 0.5um SKY130 NMOS device to ensure sufficient switching speed.
sky130_expected.reasoning: While the paper operates at 3.8 GHz using PHEMTs, a 0.5um length NMOS in SKY130 is slower. 1 GHz is chosen for reliable Class-E switching.

Output Power (Pout).description: The RF power delivered to the load at the fundamental frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Pout = 0.5768 * VDD^2 / R_load. With VDD=1.8V and R_load=1k ohm (chosen due to small W=5um), Pout = 1.86 mW = 2.7 dBm.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The extracted transistor width (5um) is extremely small for a PA, limiting the maximum current and requiring a high load impedance (1k ohm) to achieve Class-E voltage swings.

Drain Efficiency.description: The ratio of RF output power to DC input power.

sky130_expected.calculation: Ideal Class-E is 100%. Finite Ron (L=0.5um) and switching overlap losses reduce this.
sky130_expected.reasoning: At 1 GHz, the 0.5um NMOS will have moderate switching losses, yielding typical Class-E efficiencies around 60-70%.

Power Added Efficiency (PAE).description: The ratio of (RF output power - RF input power) to DC input power.

sky130_expected.calculation: PAE = (Pout - Pin) / Pdc. Pin is roughly f * Cgg * VDD^2 = 1e9 * 12.5fF * 1.8^2 = 40 uW. Since Pin << Pout (1.86 mW), PAE is close to Drain Efficiency.
sky130_expected.reasoning: High gain due to small gate capacitance means PAE will only be slightly lower than Drain Efficiency.

Power Gain.description: The ratio of RF output power to RF input power.

sky130_expected.reasoning: The device is driven by a hard square wave to act as a switch, resulting in high apparent power gain.

step3_testbench.description: Transient testbench to measure Output Power, DC Power, Drain Efficiency, and PAE of the Class-E PA at 1 GHz.
step3_testbench.spice:
* High Efficiency Broadband Class-E Power Amplifier
.lib "sky130_fd_pr/models/sky130.lib.spice" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 N5 N13 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 GND N16 N9 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}

* Terminate unused/dummy transistor XM2 to prevent floating nodes
R_N16 N16 GND 1k
R_N9 N9 GND 1k

* Class-E Load Network for XM1 (Designed for 1 GHz, Rload=1k)
Vvdd vdd GND 1.8
Lchoke vdd N5 10u
Cshunt N5 GND 20f
Lseries N5 N_mid 1.59u
Cseries N_mid out 17.9f
Rload out GND 1k

* Input Signal (1 GHz square wave for hard switching)
Vin N13 GND PULSE(0 1.8 0 10p 10p 490p 1n)

* Non-linear dependent sources to calculate instantaneous power
B_Pout Pout_node 0 V=v(out)*v(out)/1000
B_Pin Pin_node 0 V=-i(Vin)*v(N13)
B_Pdc Pdc_node 0 V=-i(Vvdd)*1.8

.control
* Run transient analysis for 40 cycles at 1 GHz
tran 10p 40n

* Measure average powers over the last 10 cycles (steady state)
meas tran Pout avg v(Pout_node) from=30n to=40n
meas tran Pin avg v(Pin_node) from=30n to=40n
meas tran Pdc avg v(Pdc_node) from=30n to=40n

* Calculate Metrics
let eff = (Pout / Pdc) * 100
let pae = ((Pout - Pin) / Pdc) * 100
let Pout_dBm = 10 * log10(Pout * 1000 + 1e-15)
let Gain_dB = 10 * log10((Pout + 1e-15) / (Pin + 1e-15))

print Pout
print Pout_dBm
print Pdc
print eff
print pae
print Gain_dB

quit
.endc
